title: Types and Parts of Vegetables in Kenya
reason: The transcript describes various activities related to vegetables and cereal crops in a classroom setting.

tasks.task: Discuss the different types of vegetables.

subtasks.text: Observe the definition of a vegetable: a plant or part of plant eaten as food when fresh.
List examples of vegetables, including tomatoes, cabbage, cucumbers, kale, and carrots.
Notice the activity to discuss the meaning of vegetables in groups.
See the group activity to present the best definition of the word vegetable to the rest of the class.

tasks.task: Describe the vegetable crops grown in Kenya.

subtasks.text: Highlight that Kenya grows many types of vegetables.
Observe the specific vegetables grown in Kenya, such as kale, cabbage, tomatoes, spinach, and onions.
Note the activity to discuss vegetables grown in students' localities and other parts of Kenya visited.
Inspect the picture to identify vegetables.

tasks.task: Explain the different types of vegetables.

subtasks.text: Classify vegetables into root, stem, and leafy vegetables.
Name the main cereal crops grown in Kenya.
Look at the photos of crops to identify cereal crops grown in different regions.
Observe the given examples of cereal crops, such as maize, rice, wheat, millet, and sogum.
Note the activity to collect and prepare cereal samples from home.

tasks.task: Cook a cereal and prepare a legume dish.

subtasks.text: Wash the rice and cook it with your parent/guardian.
Fry the beans and prepare a meal of beans with vegetables and seasoning.
